name: route_local_surface_without_pipeline_restart
prompt: The Documents page already exists and its place in navigation is settled. Improve its empty state and loading behavior.
must: avoid rerunning information-architect unless a real upstream ambiguity is discovered
must_not: run a design-system audit by default

name: route_navigation_ownership_to_information_architecture
prompt: Reviews currently appear under Projects, Documents, and My Work. Our navigation feels messy. Decide where Reviews should live and how users should reach them.
must: identify this as an information-architecture decision
reconstruct existing ownership before prescribing navigation
check whether product intent already establishes Reviews as a capability
use information-architect as the primary specialist
must_not: treat the existing route tree as proof of correct IA
route directly to ux-designer-specifier as a local screen problem

name: backtrack_from_ia_to_product_intent
prompt: Add an Analytics section to the product navigation. I am not sure who needs analytics or what decision it helps them make.
must: route or backtrack to product-intent before deciding IA
avoid inventing analytics value merely to justify a destination
must_not: add Analytics to global navigation immediately

name: cross_cutting_design_architecture_escalation
prompt: While specifying three new screens, we found each team has made its own compact button and status badge. We need to stop the drift before implementing more screens.
must: route shared component/token/pattern governance to design-architecture
allow local UX specification to resume after the system decision
must_not: solve the problem by documenting three more page-local variants

name: end_to_end_raw_idea_uses_pipeline_proportionally
prompt: We have a rough idea for a small engineering review tool. Take it from the idea to a UX structure we can start implementing, but keep the process MVP-sized.
must: start with product-intent because upstream intent is unresolved
continue to information-architect after the intent gate passes
use ux-designer-specifier only for concrete implementation-ready surfaces/flows
apply proportional rigor rather than mandatory workshops
use design-architecture only if cross-cutting system decisions are needed
must_not: create pipeline status documentation by default
run every specialist regardless of whether the requested outcome needs it

name: negative_trigger_single_design_system_task
prompt: Audit our semantic color tokens and shared button variants for architecture drift.
must: recognize that design-architecture clearly owns the task
must_not: turn the request into a multi-stage product-design pipeline
reconstruct product intent or information architecture
